Diuretic foundations: 2

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient’s blood pressure is treated with a diuretic that inhibits the sodium-chloride cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule. Which site-specific mechanism distinguishes this class from loop and collecting-duct diuretics in the nephron?

  1. NKCC2 inhibition in the thick ascending limb
  2. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism
  3. ENaC blockade in the collecting system
  4. Carbonic anhydrase inhibition
  5. NCC inhibition in the distal convoluted tubule
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

NCC inhibition in the distal convoluted tubule

Thiazides inhibit the distal sodium-chloride cotransporter.

Understanding the options

NCC inhibition in the distal convoluted tubule
Thiazides inhibit the distal sodium-chloride cotransporter.
NKCC2 inhibition in the thick ascending limb
Loop diuretics inhibit sodium-potassium-chloride transport in the thick ascending limb. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism
Spironolactone and eplerenone block aldosterone signaling and reduce potassium secretion. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
ENaC blockade in the collecting system
Amiloride and triamterene directly block epithelial sodium channels. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Carbonic anhydrase inhibition
Acetazolamide reduces bicarbonate reabsorption, predominantly in the proximal tubule. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
